debug.changelog:
fix: make the version code identical in Android Studio, terminal and CI

The version code was computed at configuration time with a raw ProcessBuilder
call, which the configuration cache cannot see as a build input. Every
environment keeps its own cache entry, so Android Studio kept reusing the value
captured when its entry was created and drifted ~40 commits behind ./gradlew
and CI builds. The native anti-tamper header then expected a different version
code than the installed APK reported, which blocked Run/Debug from the IDE.

Git output now goes through providers.exec so it is tracked as a configuration
input and recomputed whenever HEAD changes, and the version code/name are
computed once and reused by defaultConfig, the CMake flags and
generateSecurityMetadata. The native version code and version name checks are
also downgraded to log-only for debuggable builds so an incremental build can
never block debugging again.

feat: integrate AI-driven changelog generation into CI/CD

- Replaced the basic git-based changelog generation in `.woodpecker.yml` with a custom Python-based AI solution.
- Updated the `generate-changelog` CI step to use a Python 3.11 environment and install `google-generativeai`.
- Introduced `scripts/generate_ai_changelog.py` which utilizes the Gemini API to summarize commit history between tags.
- Added support for configurable AI models and custom prompts via `GEMINI_MODEL` and `CHANGELOG_PROMPT` environment variables.
- Implemented logic within the script to automatically identify the previous release tag and fetch relevant commit logs.
- Included an implementation plan and walkthrough documentation for the new integration.
